label: William J. Lynn III
narrative: Lynn is the addressee of Reid's SAP request and the decision authority who declined it. Reid's 24 June 2009 letter is addressed to 'The Honorable William Lynn III, Deputy Secretary of Defense' and asks him to establish a Restricted SAP with a bigoted access list over portions of the program. The staffing chain runs DIA technical review in October 2009, DIA memorandum finding insufficient grounds on 13 November 2009, Clapper's recommendation against on 17 November 2009, and then Lynn himself briefing Reid at 4:45pm on 19 November 2009 in Senate Visitor Center room SVC-217. The talking paper prepared for that meeting tells him to say the deliverables 'do not meet the criteria as specified in DoD 5200.1-R to justify the additional protection provided by a SAP.' Lynn was a career defense budget official — he had been DoD Comptroller under Clinton and came to the Deputy job from Raytheon, where he was senior vice president for government operations and strategy. He returned to industry after leaving in 2011.
